body_long:
Margaux Séhébiade is one of the youngest five-star hotel directors in Europe. Since 14 May 2026 she has been Hotel Manager of the Hôtel Saint-Georges in Megève, a five-star Relais & Châteaux house and the first mountain address of Chapitre Six, the French collection founded by Nicolas Saltiel.

## Three years, four houses

Her path is remarkably fast. In the summer of 2023 she worked at the front desk of the Hôtel du Palais in Biarritz, the palace of The Unbound Collection by Hyatt.

That September she joined Bertrand Hospitality as multi-site deputy manager, covering the Château des Fleurs and the Hôtel Norman, two five-star members of Small Luxury Hotels of the World. She arrived in time for the Norman's opening on 19 September 2023.

In October 2024 she became deputy director of the Château des Fleurs in Paris, then, from May 2025, deputy director of the Hôtel Norman. A year later she moved to the Alps to run her own house.

In a message shared when she took the role, she thanked Nicolas Saltiel and Nadège Ryan for their trust, and Franck Farneti and Anthony Torkington for their advice and support.

## A chalet reborn

The Saint-Georges is a historic chalet in the heart of the village. Chapitre Six reopened it on 19 December 2025, after a complete redesign by the British designer Luke Edward Hall, who built the interiors around the legend of Saint George. The original wood panelling was kept and lightened; the piano bar plays with the dragon, and Le Trappeur, the bistro led by chef Jérôme Blanchetière, takes the wild boar as its emblem.

The house has 29 keys, a piano bar that stays lively late into the night, and a wellness area built around contrast therapy, with a Japanese sauna, hot and cold baths and treatments by myBlend by Clarins. In March 2026 it joined Relais & Châteaux.

Chapitre Six now runs nine hotels in France, from Paris and Barbizon to Saint-Tropez, Cap d'Antibes and Courchevel, with a new address in Cannes due in 2027.

## The signal

Independent French groups such as Chapitre Six and Bertrand Hospitality are proving that talent can move fast. Front desk, multi-site deputy, deputy director, then a five-star house of her own: Margaux Séhébiade covered that ground in under three years.

For hoteliers, the lesson is about trust. Giving a young manager the keys to a flagship, and surrounding her with mentors, is how a group keeps its best people and gives a historic house a new energy.

Congratulations to Margaux Séhébiade and the Saint-Georges team on her first season at the helm.
summary: Hotel Manager of the Hôtel Saint-Georges in Megève since May 2026, Margaux Séhébiade runs the first mountain address of Chapitre Six, after a fast rise through Bertrand Hospitality.
title: Margaux Séhébiade, one of the youngest five-star hotel directors in Europe
why: France's new hotel groups promote on talent, not on years.
